newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Bank of Portugal rate cut to steepen yield curve.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Portugal rate cut to steepen yield curve.

text.p: The yield curve of Portuguese bonds is certain to steepen after the Bank of Portugal surprised the market by cutting its repo rate 30 basis points to 6.00 percent on Friday.
Analysts said the central bank still had room for further cuts.
"After this unexpected cut, the Bank of Portugal has room for more reductions. I see short-term money rates at five percent by the end of the year," said analyst Isabel Cabral of brokers Fincor.
"Up to the five years (bonds), yields can fall further and it is obvious that the curve is going to steepen," said Frederico Alegria do Banco ESSI.
Besides cutting its repo rate, the Bank also knocked 10 basis points off its drain and emergency lending rate, setting them at 5.7 and 7.7 percent, respectively.
Three-year bonds were gaining 17 basis points at 115.75, with the yield dipping to 5.57 percent against 5.62 percent before the rate cut was announced.
The spread with the Spanish equivalent narrowed five basis points to 20 basis points.
"The spreads (between the OT and the Bonos) are still wide and are going to have to narrow further," said Cabral.
Swap rates for the Portuguese three years fell five basis points to 5.53/60 percent.
While analysts said there was room for further rate cuts, the question was when the Bank of Portugal would opt to move again.
"The Bank may pause a little now...but it still must cut again this quarter," said Cabral.
"The point is that even after these (yield) cuts, the curve remains cheap with plenty of space for prices to gain in the short to medium part (of the curve)," said a trader.
"In the swaps, the spread between the two and 10 years in the Bund is around 224 basis points (bp) against 125 for the OT (Portuguese bonds)," said Alegria.
